## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical policy design for multi-tenant clusters and how to validate policy with real manifests.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
- image provenance, runtime security, NetworkPolicy, namespace scoping
- validation/testing workflows

## Code Example
```javascript
# ConstraintTemplate.sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
      validation: # omit for brevity
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8ssecurity
      ...
```
```javascript
# Constraint.sample
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-secure-images
spec:
  match:
    kinds: [{apiGroups: ["apps"], kinds: ["Deployment"]}]
  parameters: {registry: "registry.example.com/secure/*"}
```
```javascript
# Compliant Pod/Deployment manifest (snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/secure/app:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        volumeMounts: []
        resources: {requests: {cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi"}, limits: {cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi"}}
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

```yaml
name: Cosign Verify

          chmod +x cosign

      - name: Verify manifests images

          cosign verify registry.example.com/service@sha256:ABCDEF...
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design admission-time policy enforcement for sensitive data in multi-tenant environments. It tests understanding of tying secret handling to external stores, per-tenant encryption keys, and namespace-level controls—all critical for regulated workloads in cloud-native platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy as Code (OPA/Rego)**: Declarative policies evaluated at admission control time, enabling infrastructure teams to enforce security and compliance requirements programmatically.

- **Secrets Management**: SecretStore/CSI driver integration allows secrets to be sourced from external stores with envelope encryption using tenant-managed KMS keys, ensuring cryptographic isolation between tenants.

- **Multi-Tenancy**: Namespace-level labeling combined with EncryptionPolicy CRDs provides a declarative mechanism to enforce tenant boundaries and encryption requirements across all namespaced resources.

- **Admission Control**: Gatekeeper policies act as validation webhooks that intercept resource creation and modification requests, blocking non-compliant resources before they enter the cluster.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests advanced policy enforcement for image provenance in multi-cloud Kubernetes deployments, including runtime verification via canary tracing.

## Key Concepts
- OPA/ Gatekeeper policies for image provenance
- Docker image digests and container labels
- Canary tests and distribution across clouds
- End-to-end tracing with OTLP and trace-id linkage

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal Deployment manifest snippet
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-service
        data_version: v1.2.3
        model_version: v0.9.7
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: feature
        image: registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...
        imagePullPolicy: Always
```

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions snippet (validation)
name: Validate Provenance
on: [push]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Inspect image for digest and labels
        run: |
          CONTAINER_IMG='registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...'
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' $CONTAINER_IMG | cut -d'@' -f2)
          LABELS=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Labels}}' $CONTAINER_IMG)
          if [[ -z "$DIGEST" || "$LABELS" != *data_version* || "$LABELS" != *model_version* ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Canary trace test
        run: |
          # pseudo-step: send request and verify OTLP trace propagates
          curl -sS http://feature-service.canary/health -H 'traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-1234567812345678-01' >/dev/null
          # verification would query OTLP collector for trace-id
          echo 'Canary test passed'
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for high churn and lineage drift?
- What are the trade-offs of strict label enforcement vs. flexibility across teams?
- How would you simulate cross-cloud network latency in the gate?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a basic software supply chain gate: SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning integrated into CI, with clear pass/fail criteria.

## Key Concepts

- SBOM generation with Syft
- Vulnerability scanning with Trivy
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- Exit-code driven gates and report interpretation

## Code Example

```yaml
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t service:latest .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
      - name: Trivy scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          format: table
          exit-code: 1
```

```dockerfile
# Failing Dockerfile (vulnerable)
FROM debian:stretch-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

```dockerfile
# Passing Dockerfile (secure, updated base)
FROM debian:bullseye-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust thresholds for different environments?
- How would you add caching and parallel scans to speed up CI?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic security posture enforcement in manifests, a real-world gate that beginners can implement with standard policy engines.

## Key Concepts
- container securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities (drop ALL)
- privileged flag handling
- policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-security
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no securityContext, privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: foo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (proper securityContext)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bar
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
```

- How would you adapt the gate for multi-tenant clusters with namespace-scoped policies?
- What would you test locally to avoid CI regressions?

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in multi-cloud tenancy, data residency compliance, and automated policy enforcement. It requires understanding of cross-cloud networking, secret management patterns, service mesh security, and continuous verification using Prometheus. Candidates must demonstrate end-to-end enforcement—from namespace isolation through egress traffic, mTLS, and progressive delivery.

## Key Concepts

- **Cross-cloud tenancy isolation**: Enforcing hard boundaries between tenants across AWS, GCP, and Azure requires consistent policy engines that understand region semantics and cloud-specific resource constraints.

- **Admission control patterns**: Kyverno excels at mutation and generation, while OPA Gatekeeper provides robust enforce-or-deny semantics. Using both in concert allows for defense-in-depth.

- **Secret management**: Preventing literal secrets in environment variables and enforcing SecretStore references is critical for security compliance in regulated environments.

- **Network policy enforcement**: Per-tenant egress gateways with namespace-aware NetworkPolicies ensure traffic cannot leak across tenant boundaries.

- **Service mesh integration**: SPIRE provides automated certificate management, but admission policies must ensure workloads are properly registered before receiving traffic.

- **Progressive delivery with SLO gates**: Integrating Prometheus metrics into the deployment pipeline enables data-driven rollout decisions that protect production reliability.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests a candidate's ability to enforce governance rules on Kubernetes manifests via CI, start with beginner checks, and wire local + CI verification.

## Key Concepts

- PodDisruptionBudget basics
- Pod security via readOnlyRootFilesystem
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- local kubectl dry-run validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# failing manifest (no PDB, readOnlyRootFilesystem: false)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app-a:latest
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# passing manifest (PDB + readOnlyRootFilesystem: true)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app-a@sha256:abc
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb-svc-a
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: svc-a
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (minimal)
name: PDB + ReadOnlyRootFilesystem gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  ck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - name: Lint manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          echo 'Lint step placeholder for yamllint/jsonlint'
      - name: Validate PDB and readOnlyRootFilesystem
        run: |
          # simple validation example
          if ! kubectl get pdb pdb-svc-a >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'PDB missing for svc-a'; exit 1
          fi
          if ! grep -R "readOnlyRootFilesystem: true" -n k8s || true; then
            echo 'Some container not enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem'; exit 1
          fi
```

- How would you scale this gate to cover all namespaces and workloads beyond Deployments? 
- What are the trade-offs of enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem strictly vs allowing certain privileged ops for debugging?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-as-code skills for multi-tenant Kubernetes environments
- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

Failing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: insecure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "64Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "128Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
```

CI Validation Steps
```bash
# Install Kyverno CLI
brew install kyverno

# Validate policies against manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest deployment.yaml

# CI/CD integration example (GitHub Actions)
- name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
  run: |
    kyverno apply policy.yaml -f deploy/
```

Runtime Gate Demonstration
```bash
# Apply the policy cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Verify policy is active
kubectl get clusterpolicy require-secure-deployments

# Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest (will fail)
kubectl apply -f insecure-deployment.yaml
# Error: Validation failed: Each container must define a secure securityContext...

# Deploy compliant manifest (will succeed)
kubectl apply -f secure-deployment.yaml
# deployment.apps/secure-app created
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- SBOM generation and ingest (CycloneDX)

- Namespace labeling and non-root container policies
- CI integration and runtime verification

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simage signing
spec:
  crd: {}
  targets:
  - [' admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh','' ]
  rego: |
    package gatekeeper.image_signing
    violation["Image is not signed"] {
      input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
      not input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].image | image_signing.sign
    }
```
